An inductor with inductance `L` is placed in series with a resistor of resistance `R`, a battery of emf `epsilon`, and a switch that is initially open, as shown in the Circuit `1` diagram. The switch is closed at time `t=0`, and Circuit `1` reaches `text(half)` of its steady-state current at `t=t_1`. Circuit `2` is constructed by adding a resistor of resistance `R` in parallel with the original resistor, as shown in the Circuit `2` diagram. The switch is closed at time `t=0`, and Circuit `2` reaches `text(half)` of its steady-state current at `t=t_2`. Which of the following correctly compares `t_1andt_2`, and provides a valid justification?

A.Choice: `t_2=t_1`, because the time for an `RL` circuit to reach `text(half)` of its steady-state current only depends on `L`

B.Choice: `t_2=t_1`, because both the time constant and the steady-state current double in Circuit `2` compared to Circuit `1`

C.Choice: `t_2>t_1`, because the equivalent resistance is greater in Circuit `2` than in Circuit `1`, so the time constant is greater in Circuit `2`

D.Choice: `t_2>t_1`, because the equivalent resistance is less in Circuit `2` than in Circuit `1`, so the time constant is greater in Circuit `2`
